claim: Human difficulty of one-move matchstick arithmetic follows the scope of the constraint to be relaxed (value < operator < tautology) and chunk tightness (loose < tight). The order held in Exp 1A, 1B, 2 of the founding paper and in a 2026 online think-aloud sample (value-loose 80.7% vs tautological 19.2%, N=189).
agent_test: Build matchstick-style items with known constraint type; check the agent solve rate follows the same order. A flat order means it is not using constraint structure.
audit_note: Minor: Type A vs B difference was nonsignificant in Exp 1B/2 frequency (ceiling), and 3 of the cited Knoblich quotes are the same paper; Nasvytis 80.7/19.2 verified on arXiv HTML.

claim: The A-versus-B (value vs operator) gap is not reliably significant in solution frequency (p=.12, .14); it shows mainly in solution time, and ceiling effects hide transfer gains.
agent_test: Use solution time or tokens-to-solve, not only accuracy, when comparing operators.

claim: Restructuring transfers by representation type, not surface similarity: similarity F(3,74)=0.34 n.s.; tautology exposure did not help tight chunks (61% vs 69%, p=.64). In 2026, same-type repetition lifted accuracy 0.32 to 0.75 over 5 trials while mixed types did not.
agent_test: Store 'which representation change worked' as a typed memory; test retrieval keyed on change type vs surface similarity at equal tokens.
audit_note: Verified F(3,74)=0.34 (paper reports p=.79), 61% vs 69% chi2 p=.64, and 0.32->0.75 Same vs Different 0.32-0.39; paper notes some weak similarity effects on solution time.

claim: Eye movements fit RCT: long fixations favour values over operators early, and solvers (not non-solvers) shift attention to the crucial element late. Effect is modest (success main effect n.s., post hoc interval split), N=24.
agent_test: Not directly testable on an LLM; analogue is whether the agent treats operators as fixed when listing assumptions.

claim: Insight suddenness depends on the analysis method: ANOVA on time bins hid a late abrupt attention shift that GAM and change-point models found (N=61, 34% solved in 5 min, 45% after a hint).
agent_test: Method warning for any aha detection on agent traces: use change-point models, not binned means.

claim: Progress monitoring is a live rival: a large value disparity nearly erased the tight-chunk penalty (high-value 77% tight vs 90% loose; low-value 43% vs 77%) and raised standard tautology solving from 12% to 62%. The chunk effect partly replicated; necessity of constraint relaxation is doubted. Gap-search check: numbers verified from the full text (Ormerod & MacGregor 2020, N=121 and 133 analysed). The paper argues relaxation is unnecessary; that is its reading, and no model test exists.
agent_test: Ablate: representation-change operator vs a progress-monitoring trigger (switch when distance to goal stalls) at equal tokens.

claim: Nine-dot and eight-coin difficulty has several interacting sources (perceptual, knowledge, process). Training that removed the hidden constraint (turn at a non-dot point) helped (63% vs 37%, N=90); misleading training did not hurt (probable floor). Gap-search check: unaided nine-dot is about 0% (MacGregor et al 2001, cited in Kershaw 2004); trained groups reach 30 to 97% depending on the number of non-dot turns.
agent_test: Give the agent targeted 'which assumption is hidden' prompts; compare with generic hints at equal tokens.
audit_note: Verified 63% vs 37% N=90 (Kershaw&Ohlsson 2001, test problems were nine-dot variants, hindering 27% numerically lower, authors cite floor effect) and trained 30-97%, unaided ~0% (Kershaw 2004).

claim: Move choice follows the current representation more than heuristics: representational change required predicts two-move and eight-coin difficulty; heuristics have minimal effect. Evidence is from abstracts only.
agent_test: Verify full text first. Test: forced re-representation before search vs more search at equal tokens.

claim: Most solvers do not follow the classic four-stage insight order; search and impasse recur. Self-reported insight (74% of solvers vs 10% of non-solvers) is subjective.
agent_test: Do not hard-code one impasse-then-restructure sequence; allow looping.

claim: Most frontier LLMs are far below humans on insight-style restructuring items: NazoNazo 7.6% (non-reasoning) and 17.6% (reasoning) vs human 52.9% (95% CI 46.6 to 59.2), but GPT-5 fell inside the human interval (descriptive, no formal test). BRAINTEASER ChatGPT (2023): sentence 62.68 overall, word 53.46, falling to 39.71 and 29.27 when the original and both rewordings must all be right; humans 91.98 and 91.67. No 2025 reasoning-model consistency numbers were found.
agent_test: Run scaffold vs plain on NazoNazo and BRAINTEASER with reconstruction consistency at equal tokens.

claim: Many LLM failures on restructuring items are verification failures: the right candidate appears in the thought log but is not committed (5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers, 4 models, string match). Gap-search check: the 5.23 to 39.34% table exists only in NazoNazo v3 (v1 and v2 are qualitative). Recovering every failure would lift Grok 4 from 37% to 62% correct and Gemini from 14% to 19% (upper bounds, string match).
agent_test: Add a candidate-harvest-and-select step over the thought log; measure recovered accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace Aha shifts in small RL-trained models are rare (6.31% of traces) and go with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%). A second generation with an appended reconsideration cue gives +8.41 pp on math (32.21 to 40.62, N=320,000 pairs, Qwen2.5-1.5B family) but +0.45 on crosswords and +0.01 on Rush Hour. The gain is larger when Pass-1 entropy was high (math +15.38 vs +5.82), but that bucket is selected on a low-accuracy Pass 1, so part is regression to the mean. A cue-free second sample at equal tokens was never run.
agent_test: Compare entropy-triggered forced re-representation with a plain resample at equal tokens on math and a puzzle set.

claim: Red herrings cause fixation-like failure in LLMs: on Only Connect grouping, GPT-4 0-shot solved 6 walls (239 correct groups) on OCW vs 471 walls (1926 groups) on OCW-WordNet, a synthetic set without red herrings (knowledge content also differs); 1 to 10 in-context examples did not improve grouping (Task 1); the best model fully solves 18% of NYT Connections games (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Samadarshi et al.).
agent_test: Test a 'name the tempting wrong frame, then exclude it' step on Connections-style tasks at equal tokens.
audit_note: Naeini: in-context examples did not help only on Task 1 (grouping); on Task 2 (connections) GPT-4 improved monotonically with more examples. Also 6/239 are solved walls/correct groups on OCW, 471/1926 on OCW-WordNet (no red herrings, different content).
claim_before_audit: Red herrings cause fixation-like failure in LLMs: removing misleading groups raises GPT-4 from 6/239 to 471/1926 groups (knowledge also changes); best model fully solves 18% of Connections games; more in-context examples did not help.

claim: On matchstick equations VLMs do poorly (o3 60.00% with text, 38.50% without; humans 91.72%); sign-changed items are harder for every model. Seven-segment digits are used, so chunk theory is untested.
agent_test: Re-test MathSticks with a constraint-listing step (value/operator/tautology) vs plain.

claim: Mental-set tests on LLMs (6 problems per cell) show fallback to the familiar method and CoT raising accuracy at 3 steps instead of 1. Too small to conclude anything.
agent_test: Treat as anecdote; repeat with 50+ items per cell.

claim: External reformulation can help without the model restructuring itself: restart with story plus selected answers won 4/5 vs 2/5 on situation puzzles; rewording wrongly answered math items recovered up to 15.5 pp but lacked a resample control.
agent_test: Compare scaffold-driven reformulation against plain resampling at equal token cost.

claim: Machine constraint relaxation works in optimisation: AutoCO cut optimality gap 24.7% vs LLM baselines. An LLM agent proposing alternative constraint models improved 68.5% of cases, but best-of-5 (101/150) matched the agent (about 102.8/150).
agent_test: Always include a best-of-k arm at equal budget when claiming relaxation gains.
audit_note: Verified 1028/1500 (68.5%), best-of-5 101/150 vs agent 102.8, AutoCO 24.7% average optimality-gap reduction vs SOTA LLM methods (abstract-level claim).

claim: Two-agent GPT-4o teams on situation puzzles asked more varied questions yet solved worse than solo; 47% of the deficit came via fewer host questions.
agent_test: Caution against coordination overhead; not applicable to a single agent.

claim: Verbal insight problems: ChatGPT solved 12/30 classic items (within the likely human range, single run, contamination risk) but is worse than humans on a rebus representational-change task and reasons where humans transform. Gap-search check: contamination is better handled by NazoNazo-style blind items than by classic problems; no uncontaminated classic-insight LLM test was found.
agent_test: Rerun with repeated sampling on uncontaminated items.

claim: No executable RCT model exists in any opened source; RCT predictions are rank orders only.
agent_test: Implement a small constraint/chunk simulator to generate predicted difficulty orders to compare with LLM prompts.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: BRAINTEASER ChatGPT exact scores (zero-shot, 2023): sentence Original 60.77, Semantic 59.33, Context 67.94, all three right in a group 39.71, overall 62.68; word 56.10, 52.44, 51.83, group 29.27, overall 53.46. Humans 91.98 and 91.67 (102 items). The earlier 53 vs 63 disagreement was word vs sentence overall.
agent_test: Report the group-consistency metric, not the mean, when comparing a scaffold with plain prompting.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Progress monitoring vs representation change has been compared only in humans (Ormerod & MacGregor 2020; Jones 2003 cited, not opened). No LLM trace study separates the two, so the head-to-head is untested.
agent_test: Label each trace for stall-then-switch and for changed representation; regress success on both at equal tokens.

claim: Searches found no LLM study that (a) pits an explicit constraint-list-then-relax step against sampling and best-of-k on matchsticks, (b) tests the Knoblich difficulty order in LLM solve rates, (c) provides an executable RCT simulator, or (d) tests memory keyed by representation-change type. MathSticks (seven-segment, o3 60.00% with text) is the closest and has a public generator. Search budget ran out, so this is absence in a limited search.
agent_test: Build the Roman-numeral matchstick generator with tagged constraint and chunk types; run plain, best-of-k, and constraint-list arms at equal tokens, holding number disparity fixed.

claim: Number disparity is a confound for any difficulty-order test: with a large value gap, standard-tautology solving rose from 12% to 62% and the tight-chunk penalty shrank (77% vs 90%). Control disparity when testing O4 or O6 on matchsticks.
agent_test: Match items on disparity across constraint types, or include disparity as a factor.

claim: Oellinger 2006 (N=120), Oellinger 2014 and Ohlsson 1992/2011 remain known only through abstracts and secondary text; heuristics-have-minimal-effect (K08) stays unverified.
agent_test: Obtain full texts before citing numbers.
